name: Noxus
one_line: Configurable agents that use flows, integration actions, knowledge bases, tables, MCP servers, code execution and a sandbox to carry out tasks, deployed through the web app, API, SDK, chat widget, Slack, Teams, Google Chat, WhatsApp or Telegram.

gamma_ray.fact_ray: 25 facts: 25 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: Noxus's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)

configs.what: Noxus AI Workers (AI Co-workers; 'Agents' in the documentation) with its documented defaults.
Code Execution tool turned on for the agent
Sandbox tool turned on for the agent (persistent Syd sandbox)
Human in the Loop tool or Require Approval turned on for the agent
Agent deployed under a service account or app-only identity rather than a user's OAuth
Phoenix or Langfuse observability provider connected, enabling user feedback on responses
Integration actions (single integration nodes, such as Send Email or Delete OneDrive File) selected as tools for the agent

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: The tools page states one agent can be given integration actions as tools, such as Send Email, Create Google Drive Sharing Link or Delete OneDrive File, alongside flows, knowledge bases and database connections.
facts.quote: Create Google Drive Sharing Link or Delete OneDrive File

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: The tools page documents a Human in the Loop tool an agent owner may enable, under which the agent escalates to a person to get approval for critical actions; it does not say how any given agent is shipped.

facts.label: It exposes an agent interface: a published MCP server, an agent card, or an API documented for agents to call
facts.fact: A hosted MCP server lets external clients and agents call Noxus agents, conversations and workflows as tools, authenticated with a workspace API key whose permissions gate the tools.
facts.quote: Drive the Noxus platform from any MCP-compatible client

facts.label: It asks for narrower access than the whole account
facts.fact: Each agent reaches only the flows, actions, knowledge bases and database connections selected for it; its SQL is generated read-only and runs with that connection's privileges, and tables are read-only unless edits are allowed.
facts.quote: Select which database connection(s) the agent may query

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: The Human in the Loop tool and Require Approval make the agent ask a person before actions run.

facts.label: What it can reach is enumerated: scopes, permissions, tools
facts.fact: Each agent's tools are an enumerated list chosen by the builder: the flows, actions, knowledge bases, database connections and MCP servers it may use.
facts.quote: Select which flows the agent can access

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The tools page documents limits, such as web research being less reliable than knowledge bases.
facts.quote: Web research is slower and less reliable than knowledge bases.

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The tools page describes the data an agent can use: knowledge bases, connected databases queried read-only, and workspace tables.
facts.quote: Query, and optionally edit, workspace tables

facts.label: The models and third-party components it uses are listed
facts.fact: The model providers and model families an agent can use are listed.

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Noxus's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
